verdicts.claim: Whether a seller may change the craft of a live listing is specified both ways: 05.01.01 blocks it as immutable, 05.01.02 permits it. Neither statement carries a marker or references the other.
verdicts.reason: All quotes verbatim. 05.01.01-service-listings-packages-rate-cards.md:191 D-10 'Craft is immutable on a live listing — archive and republish'; :82 'Seller changes the craft of a live listing (Mixing -> Mastering) | Blocked. ... "You can't change the craft of a live listing. Archive it and publish a new one"'. Directly against 05.01.02-service-category-taxonomy-attributes.md:105 'Seller edits craft on a listing with accumulated reputation | ... The edit is permitted; the reputation does not follow | "Reviews stay with the work you did. This listing starts fresh in Mastering."' — and reinforced a second time at 05.01.02:157 'reputation is per-role (05.01.01 DT-03), which is why a craft edit does not carry reviews across crafts'. Both files are [DEEP] (status headers verified). A domain-wide grep for craft-mutability language returns only these lines — no CX row, index decision or marker reconciles them, and neither file cites the other's outcome. Both supply finished user-facing copy for the same Mixing-to-Mastering example with opposite outcomes, so the two statements cannot both hold and an implementer must invent the rule. (05.01.02:95's 'Listing's craft changes while a quote derived from it is live' is weaker — it plausibly describes a taxonomy-side merge, not a seller edit — so it is excluded from the upheld evidence.)

verdicts.claim: The domain CX file resolves the capacity-vs-immutable-offer collision by making the concurrency ceiling block quote issuance; both owning features specify that it does not — it binds ordering only, and issuance merely surfaces an advisory exposure figure.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the two readings collapse into one build. Quotes are verbatim but the capacity counter's basis reconciles them: services-marketplace-cx.md:137 defines the count as the accepted-engagement count ('Acceptance of a live offer always succeeds and increments the accepted-engagement count; issuance of a new quote is what the ceiling blocks'). Under that definition 05.02.01-custom-quotes-proposals-scope.md:112 is fully consistent — it addresses only acceptance ('Seller is at their concurrency ceiling when the buyer accepts | Acceptance is not blocked'), and its own copy proves the mechanism: 'You're now at 5 of 4 concurrent. Two quotes are still live — withdraw them?' i.e. the over-ceiling state arises from concurrent acceptances of quotes issued while under ceiling, exactly as CX-12 describes. 05.02.01:68 listing the ceiling under 'Does not end the offer' is the same point (existing offers survive), and the :77 exposure figure is coherent as the advisory warning against precisely that oversubscription. The claimed self-contradiction at services-marketplace-cx.md:139 is a misreading: it says the seller is warned 'when near capacity', while :137 blocks at capacity — near and at are different states, not contradictory ones. 05.01.07:94 D-03 ('At-capacity listings stay visible and non-orderable') governs the Order CTA and does not assert anything about issuance. No divergent build.

verdicts.claim: 05.02.01 D-15 requires the benchmark band to render to both parties on a live quote; 05.01 decided sellers-only and rejected the buyer-facing pairing three times. Neither side flags the other.
verdicts.reason: All quotes verbatim. 05.02.01-custom-quotes-proposals-scope.md:244 D-15 'The benchmark band (05.01.04) is rendered on a live quote symmetrically to both parties, or to neither'. The 'or to neither' escape is foreclosed by the same file twice: :77 has the issuing seller seeing 'the benchmark band for this craft/cohort (05.01.04, symmetric — D-15)', and its Cross-Cut Notes at :192 state flatly 'the band is rendered on a live quote symmetrically to both parties (D-15)'. Against 05.01.01:186 D-05 'renders in the seller's pricing step only — never in the buyer preview or on the public listing'; 05.01.04-rate-benchmarking-price-transparency.md:96 Q-03 'RESOLVED — 05.01.01 D-05 ... Sellers only', which explicitly names 'Buyer viewing a quote sees the same band' as text the decision supersedes — i.e. the quote surface is the exact case decided against; 05.01-service-listings-pricing-cx.md:89 R-04 and services-marketplace-cx.md:216 R-06 repeat it. 05.02.01 and 05.01.01 are both [DEEP]. A domain-wide grep for D-15/'symmetric' shows no file reconciling the two: 05.02.01 never cites D-05, R-04 or R-06, and the 05.01 side never cites D-15. Two implementers diverge on whether a buyer evaluating a quote sees the cohort band.

verdicts.claim: Whether a credit is emitted at milestone acceptance is decided in both directions across sibling features, and each cites the other as its authority. Under one reading a cancelled staged engagement emits duplicate credits.
verdicts.reason: All quotes verbatim, and the conflict is between two [DEEP] files, not merely against a [PARTIAL] one. 05.06.03-rights-transfer-split-execution.md ([DEEP]):59 'Milestone acceptance (05.03.02) | Tranche release | Does not execute ... | Emits — a credit is a fact about work that happened (05.03.05 D-06)', :61 'Milestone acceptance is therefore a two-leg commit (money + credit)', :131 'Releases the tranche and emits the credit'. Against 05.03.05-cancellation-abandonment-kill-fee.md ([DEEP]):274 D-06, whose rationale asserts in the present tense 'no credit is emitted at a milestone at all (05.06.03 D-01 fires emission at final acceptance)', restated at :302 'Credits were never emitted at milestones at all.' 05.06.03:59 cites 05.03.05 D-06 as its authority for milestone emission while 05.03.05 D-06 denies that mechanism — a mutual mis-citation. The duplicate-emission harm is concrete: 05.03.05:108/:151 (DT-11) have the cancelled engagement emit credits for accepted milestones at the elected visibility, while 05.06.03:130 has them merely 'stand' (already emitted). Building both double-emits every accepted stage into domain 02. 05.03.05:251 flags only the adjacent rights-leg separability question ('DT-11 asserts that credit emission is separable from the rights leg ... must be checked'), not the emission trigger, so nothing tracks this. Emission trigger for the platform's core asset must be invented.

verdicts.claim: The engagement state machine's trigger for Closed is the recall window expiring, while the same file's happy path and the recall feature both put the engagement in Closed with the window still open — and the state is defined as read-only, which makes recalls impossible.
verdicts.reason: UPHELD but overstated. The internal contradiction is real and sits inside one [DEEP] file: 05.03.01-order-lifecycle-requirements-gating.md:157 'Closed | Support/recall window expired (05.03.06) | Read-only; evidence retained.' against :101 '10. Engagement enters Closed, with the support/recall window still open (05.03.06).' The states table (verified :148-159) has no intervening state — Accepted (:156) then Closed (:157) — so the two readings put the engagement in different states for the whole window, a user-visible difference. Downgraded because the second half of the claim is refuted and the majority reading is discernible: 05.03.06-post-delivery-support-recall.md:87 D-01 'A recall is a post-terminal state — the engagement stays closed, rights stay transferred, escrow stays released' and 05.03-engagement-lifecycle-index.md:50 D-02 'a recall must reopen a closed engagement without unwinding its rights transfer' both align with :101, making 3-to-1 in favour of Closed-at-acceptance. D-01's post-terminal framing also defeats the 'read-only makes recalls impossible' argument — the recall is a distinct post-terminal object, not an edit to the engagement record. So the residual defect is a wrong trigger cell, not an unbuildable feature.

verdicts.claim: The spec pricing model has no legal rights-posture combination, and its conditional vesting cannot be expressed in the closed posture vocabulary — yet a posture election is mandatory before a listing tier can publish.
verdicts.reason: UPHELD but overstated. Quotes verbatim: 05.01.03-music-pricing-model-library.md:43 defines Spec ('renders from nothing', 'trigger condition · the term that vests on trigger', 'No — conditional (DT-10)'), :150 DT-10 rejects spec-as-points; 05.06.01-engagement-rights-posture.md:70-74 has exactly three rows (Cash-only, Points-only, Fee + points), :208 D-07 closes the vocabulary, :202 D-01 'No default posture — an explicit election is required to publish a tier'. A grep confirms zero mentions of the spec model anywhere in 05.06, and 05.06.01 Q-07 (:226) tracks reversion, not spec, while 05.01.03 Q-07 (:206) tracks only who detects the vesting trigger. Downgraded on two grounds. First, the legal-combinations table is demonstrably class-level, not a per-model enumeration — Half-day, Hourly, Retainer and Buyout are also absent and fold trivially into Cash-only — so its silence on spec is weaker evidence of a locked contradiction than claimed. Second, publish is not actually blocked: a spec listing can elect a posture (the 'term that vests on trigger' is a posture), and 05.01.03 Q-07 already presupposes exactly that by asking who notifies the spec engagement so the term can vest. The residual real gap is narrower than stated — whether a posture may execute on a future trigger rather than at acceptance is unstated and untracked — which is a warning, not a publish-blocker.

verdicts.claim: A below-scale union render is specified as auto-raised to the floor and as blocked, in the same file, for the same trigger — including inside a single table cell.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the same file's states table supplies the two-branch model the claim says is missing. 05.01.03-music-pricing-model-library.md:131 'Floored | Union scale exceeds the rendered fee | Price raised to scale with the reason and the session type named' and :132 'Blocked | Below a statutory or union floor, or an out-of-range input' are distinct states, and :104 settles the exact scenario in the claim with finished copy: 'Union scale exceeds the seller's own rate | The floor wins. ... "Your rate is £400; AFM scale for a master session is £480. Priced at £480."' So auto-flooring is decided for the render path. :76 states the branch rule explicitly ('raised to the floor with the reason shown, or issue is blocked'), and :103's terse second clause is the residual case reachable only when flooring does not apply (manual issue below scale, blocked per 05.02.01/05.02.03). Two competent implementers converge: floor the render, refuse a below-scale issue. The auditor concedes the reconciliation in their own forcedInvention text.

verdicts.claim: The universal publish-gate parameters are stated to apply to every pricing model regardless of shape, which makes a points-only or spec listing unpublishable, contradicting the feature's own thesis that those shapes exist.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the prose at 05.01.03:49 cites '(D-03, D-04, D-05)' and those decisions scope themselves, which is the reader's route. Verified: :186 D-04 'Every cash model declares currency and tax treatment' explicitly narrows two of the four parameters to cash models, so the currency/tax half of the claim is answered in the same file's decision log. The remaining two are expressible for non-cash shapes: :185 D-03's minimum ('The rate is marketing; the minimum is the business') applies to a minimum points percentage, and :187 D-05 requires the rounding rule 'declared per model' — a per-model declaration, not a cash concept forced onto a rights term. The parameter table (:53-56) likewise attaches Currency to 'the seller's payout currency' and Tax treatment to 'rendered figures', both cash-scoped by construction. No implementer is driven to supply meaningless values or to conclude a points-only listing cannot publish.

verdicts.claim: 05.01.04's normative Role Lens and Happy Path still specify a buyer-visible benchmark band, which the sellers-only decision supersedes; the correction is recorded only in a resolved-question row, not at the point of use.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED as a tracked deferral. The stale text exists verbatim (05.01.04-rate-benchmarking-price-transparency.md:18 'Sees the same band as a buyer when evaluating a quote'; :37 'Buyer viewing a quote sees the same band'), but the same file's Q-03 at :96 names both lines specifically, states the governing decision, and assigns the correction to a named stage: 'its Musician Role Lens ... and Happy Path step 5 ... are breadth-pass text that the later [DEEP] decision supersedes — they should be corrected at /write-fe-spec when the pricing-step surface is specified.' The file's status header is [PARTIAL], i.e. it declares its own incomplete depth. A superseded-text notice with the superseding decision cited and a target stage is the documented mechanism, and it sits in the same file an implementer is reading. The substantive disagreement about buyer visibility is real but belongs to the 05.02.01 D-15 finding, which is upheld separately; this finding is only about marker placement.

verdicts.claim: Percentage add-on composition is untestable as written: they are declared to apply to the subtotal yet also to apply in declared order, which are different arithmetic for two or more percentage add-ons.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the base is named explicitly, which removes the compounding reading. 05.01.01:43 restricts an add-on's pricing model to '{flat, same-unit-as-tier, percentage-of-subtotal}': the model's own name fixes the base as the subtotal, not the running total, so rush +50% and Atmos x1.5 each compute against the same 1,000 and the order of the two percentages is immaterial (2,000). ':38 applied to the subtotal in declared order' is consistent with this — declared order governs where flat and same-unit add-ons land relative to the subtotal, which is exactly the non-commutativity :33 asserts ('Add-ons occur in the real market in three shapes and they do not commute' — three shapes, not two percentages). The 2,250 reading requires ignoring the 'percentage-of-subtotal' model name. Exact evaluation-order arithmetic is in any case BE-pricing-spec detail rather than vision-layer product behaviour.

verdicts.claim: At Capacity is specified only as disabling the Order CTA; whether an at-capacity seller may still receive a quote request and issue a quote is unstated in both the capacity feature and the listing state machine, while the domain CX asserts the ceiling gates quote issuance.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED by the finding's own evidence — the answer is one file over. services-marketplace-cx.md:137 decides issuance at capacity ('issuance of a new quote is what the ceiling blocks. Failure surfaces at issuance ("you're at capacity")'), which is the CX file's designated job for a cross-feature rule between 05.01 and 05.02. The at-capacity affordance is also positively specified rather than merely omitted: 05.01.07-seller-capacity-queue-intake-limits.md:64 and 05.01.01:117 both give 'waitlist CTA, next-available date' as what replaces ordering, so the waitlist is the stated route for a buyer who wants work from an at-capacity seller. The contrast drawn with 05.01.01:116 ('Request Quote only, Order disabled') is a different state with a different cause (payout incomplete, where quoting is the point). No product behaviour must be invented.

verdicts.claim: An Action needed listing state is defined in 05.01.02 and made load-bearing by its 30-day pause countdown, but is absent from the listing lifecycle state machine that 05.01.01 owns, and the two files describe its orderability differently.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the behaviour is fully specified where it is declared, and the orderability halves reconcile. 05.01.02:118 defines the row inside 05.01.02's own states table (verified :110-118, whose other rows are Loading/Populated/Empty/Partial/Error surface states), and the row is deliberately tagged '(listing)' to mark it as the one listing-scoped entry; :93 supplies the full behaviour — stay live under the old label, seller notified day 0/7/28, day-30 pause, and it names Paused as 'an existing 05.01.01 state', showing the author knew which states 05.01.01 owns. 'Stay live' and 05.01.03:116's 'new orders are gated pending remap' are not in conflict: 05.01.01's own machine distinguishes live-and-orderable from live-and-not-orderable (:116 'Live and discoverable; "Request Quote" only, Order disabled'), so live-but-gated is an existing shape. What remains is that the state name is not mirrored into 05.01.01's lifecycle table — spec hygiene, not forced invention; an implementer has complete behaviour and would converge on it whether modelled as a state or a flag.

verdicts.claim: A money-affecting escrow rule is left with a bare [PENDING] carrying neither an owner nor a deferral target.
verdicts.reason: Verified verbatim at services-marketplace-cx.md:104 (CX-06 synthesis Q5) and repeated at 05.05-multi-party-supply-cx.md:73, both ending in a bare '`[PENDING]`' with no owner and no stage. A domain-wide grep for 'per-payee|whole-escrow|payee freeze|partial freeze' returns only those two lines, confirming no open question, index row or leaf feature owns it. The tracking is malformed rather than merely pending: every open question in this domain's Q tables carries Owner and Deferred To columns (e.g. 05.06.02:122-125, 05.07.02:105-108), so a synthesis item with neither has no route to being decided. Weight comes from the file's own status header — services-marketplace-cx.md is '[DEEP] — 7 sub-domains, deepening pass c...', a claim of completed synthesis, so an unowned open item inside it is not covered by a declared-incomplete status. Escrow freeze granularity (per-payee vs whole-escrow) determines when a buyer's release is held hostage to a third party's dispute.

verdicts.claim: Two [DEEP] files specify different, incompatible nudge schedules for the same requirements-gate stall, and the second calls its day-7 notice the first nudge.
verdicts.reason: Quotes verbatim and both files are [DEEP]. 05.03.01-order-lifecycle-requirements-gating.md:107 'Buyer nudged at T+24h, T+72h, T+7d, T+14d; then 05.03.05's escalating abandonment notice', repeated in its Consumes list at :211 as 'gate nudges (T+24h/72h/7d/14d)'. Against 05.03.05-cancellation-abandonment-kill-fee.md:121-124, whose buyer-side table is '7 | First nudge — informational | Buyer only', '14 | Second nudge | Both.', '30 | Abandonment Notice', '45 | Auto-Close', with D-04 (:272) restating '7/14/30 notices, close at 45'. The delegation does not cover this: 05.03.01 D-12 (:232) delegates only the threshold — 'The gate reports elapsed-since-open; 05.03.05 owns the threshold' — and :194 sets the boundary as 'the gate observes, cancellation decides', while :20 keeps nudge-sending with the gate ('the platform holds the gate and sends the nudges'). The two cadences overlap at days 7 and 14 (duplicate notifications) and cannot both be first. One implementer ships six buyer touches, another four. Warning-level: notification cadence, no money or rights consequence.

verdicts.claim: The domain CX assigns the retainer feature a pinned-rate flag that protects a contracted rate from rate-card mutation; 05.03.04 contains no such flag, no pinning rule, and no reference to the listing feature at all.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the absence is confirmed but it is not a spec gap. Verified: services-marketplace-cx.md:24 CX-13 'A contracted retainer rate is PINNED against rate-card bulk mutation' and :151 'the retainer exposes a pinned-rate flag and the card's blast radius must exclude any listing under an active retainer'; a programmatic scan of 05.03.04-retainers-recurring-engagements.md returns 0 matches for 'pin', 0 references to 05.01.01 and 0 for 'rate card'. But CX-13's synthesis is complete on its own terms — :151-155 specify the owner split, the pre-commit enumeration, the permission rule, the warning and the race resolution — and a domain CX file is the designated carrier for an obligation spanning two features, which is exactly the 'detail carried one file over' case. The rate-card side also carries the flag (05.01.01 pinned-by-contract field). 05.03.04 is [SURFACE], so its thin Cross-Cut Notes (05.01.03, 05.01.07, 05.05.01 only) reflect a declared un-deepened state rather than a contradiction. The residual defect is a missing back-reference.

verdicts.claim: The notes-window duration is given as a flat 48h (24h on rush) in a decision and as a per-craft value as low as 24h in the seed table, with no rule for how rush interacts with a craft whose seed is already 24h.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the interaction rule is stated and deterministic. 05.03.03-revisions-limits-change-orders.md:81 'Rush inheritance: if a rush tier is bought (05.01.06), the revision turnaround inherits the rush tier and the notes window halves' — 'halves' is an operation on whatever the seed is, so rush mastering-single resolves to 12h from the table's 24h with no ambiguity. The file also routes the reader explicitly: :38 'Seed default 48 hours (24h on any rush tier — see the per-craft table below)', and :227 D-15 makes the per-craft table the seed source, 'seller-overridable in both directions — a starting value, never a cap or a floor'. D-08's '(48h; 24h on rush)' at :220 is the modal-craft illustration consistent with halving 48h. The claimed three-way ambiguity (24/12/24) dissolves once 'halves' is applied to the craft seed, which is the only reading the text supports.

verdicts.claim: The absolute rule that a QC-failing file never reaches the buyer and never starts their clock is stated without exception in two places, and contradicted by the seller-override path specified in the owning QC feature and acknowledged in the same file's happy path.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the state vocabulary separates the two outcomes and the owning file carries the exception at the point of use. 05.04.02-deliverable-spec-automated-audio-qc.md:76 defines a distinct 'Overridden | Seller overrides with a reason | Buyer sees the override and the reason at delivery' state alongside :106 D-04 and :59 ('Override with a reason, recorded and shown to the buyer. Never a silent bypass'), while 05.04.01-delivery-acceptance-auto-accept.md:152 scopes its prohibition to the 'QC Failed' state ('Seller only'). An overridden file is therefore not in the QC Failed state that D-01 (:210) and index D-02 (:46) speak about — those govern an unoverridden failure, whose whole point is that the seller must act. 05.04.01's own happy path at :96 states the branch explicitly: 'it passes (or the seller overrides with a recorded reason, which the buyer will see)'. Two implementers converge: QC fail blocks; override converts it to a disclosed delivery.

verdicts.claim: Mid-chain cancellation settlement across a bundle's sellers, and the terminal Broken state for a seller exiting mid-chain, are both left [PENDING] with no owner and no open question covering them.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED on two independent grounds, one of which the auditor concedes. First, 05.05-multi-party-supply-index.md:47 D-03 disposes of the whole feature: 'Multi-Seller Bundles retained as a node but proposed `wont` for MoSCoW', with 05.05.04:74 DT-02 named as 'the concrete basis for the `wont` proposal rather than a vague "too complex"' — settlement arithmetic for a feature explicitly staged out of v1 is not a gap an implementer hits. Second, 05.05.04-multi-seller-bundles-curated-packages.md carries status [SURFACE] (header verified), i.e. it declares that Step 5 deepening has not run; the bare '`[PENDING]`' rows at :54, :55 and :67 are the expected breadth-pass state of an un-deepened file, and the file-level status is the tracking. A MoSCoW disposition plus a declared depth level are both documented mechanisms.

verdicts.claim: Whether an elected points participation survives a re-recording of the work is marked [PENDING] with no owner, no deferral target and no covering open question.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the file declares its own incomplete depth. 05.06.02-producer-points-backend-participation.md:62 'Points on a recording later re-recorded | The 2020s' favourite manoeuvre | `[PENDING]`' is verbatim, and Q-01..Q-04 (verified :122-125) indeed cover other subjects. But the file's status header is [PARTIAL], not [DEEP] — deepening is declared partially done, so an edge-case row still carrying the bare open-item marker falls inside the scope the status already flags as unfinished. Bare '`[PENDING]`' is this domain's consistent house shorthand for an open edge case (present in ~15 rows across 05.01.04, 05.02.03, 05.03.02, 05.03.04, 05.05.03, 05.06.05, 05.07.01/02/03), so its use here is convention rather than a lost requirement. This is materially weaker than the same complaint against the [DEEP] domain CX (per-payee freeze), which is upheld precisely because that file claims completed synthesis.

verdicts.claim: A defect warranty on custodial labour is named as a trade norm with a range instead of a platform behaviour, and nothing decides whether the platform implements one or for how long.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — depth is not yet due for this unit. The quote is verbatim (05.07.01-repair-tech-luthier-job-flow.md:59 'Warranty on the work | Trade norm: 6-12 months on labour | Different from a mix recall (05.03.06) — this is a defect warranty on physical work'), and a grep confirms no decision in 05.07 addresses repair-labour warranty (05.07.02:99 D-05 covers only the inspector, 'not a warranty or an insurer'). But every file in the sub-domain is [SURFACE] and 05.07-custodial-physical-services-index.md is [SURFACE], with services-marketplace-index.md:39 recording 05.07 as '[BREADTH]' — naming a trade norm and its distinction from the creative recall is exactly what a breadth-pass edge-case row is for, and deciding the platform behaviour is what the deepening pass does. The comparison drawn with 05.03.06's bounded window is not like-for-like: that file was deepened. Demanding a locked decision from an explicitly un-deepened unit is a category error, and the status marker is the tracking.

verdicts.claim: Two behaviours are left with bare [PENDING] markers that carry no owner and no deferral target, and no open question in the unit covers either.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED for the same depth reason, and one half is explicitly stage-tracked. Both quotes are verbatim (05.07-custodial-physical-services-cx.md:41 return-damage vs in-progress precedence, '`[PENDING]`'; 05.07.02-third-party-inspection-verification.md:67 'Disputed | Report contested | `[PENDING]`'). But 05.07.02 is [SURFACE] and the same file at :54 carries a properly stage-tagged marker for exactly this subject — 'Report contested by the gear seller | It cost them a sale | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — right of reply?' — naming both the open question and the stage that resolves it, which is the documented mechanism. The 05.07 CX file belongs to a sub-domain whose index and all three leaves are [SURFACE] (services-marketplace-index.md:39 records it as [BREADTH]), so its synthesis is at breadth depth by declaration, unlike the [DEEP] domain CX. The contrast with 05.05.01:112 D-05 and 05.03.05 D-16 resolving similar races is a contrast with deepened units.
